note: Makes constraints_on fuzzy: when exact-norm match fails and a fuzzy_bar is set, scans all candidates and returns the best match above the bar. The decision-rewording bench (docs/decision-rewording-bench.md N1) measured this: StringMatcher rank@1 is 88% on re-worded decisions, but the 0.92 seal bar blocks all of them. At 0.45, recall is 75% with 0 wrong-key on 24 distinct decisions. On the full 418-decision dogfood corpus, the triage calibrate found 0.55 as the knee (below that, question-scaffold false positives flood). Default is 0.55 for the CLI, configurable via --fuzzy-bar.

decisions.question: Should constraints_on do fuzzy matching when exact-norm match fails?
decisions.commitment: Yes — constraints_on now accepts a fuzzy_bar parameter. When exact-norm match via memory_find fails and fuzzy_bar is set (and >0), it scans all candidates with the matcher and returns the highest-scoring one above the bar. The result dict now includes 'match' ('exact'|'fuzzy'|'none') and 'similarity' fields so callers can see how the match was made. A fuzzy match also includes 'matched_question' in the live dict so the caller sees the actual stored question.
decisions.why: The rewording bench (N1, docs/decision-rewording-bench.md) established that the bar was the defect, not the matcher. StringMatcher puts the correct decision at rank 1 for 88% of re-worded queries — but the 0.92 seal bar blocks all of them. A calibrated bar (~0.45–0.55) recovers 54–75% with 0 false constraints. The fix was in the box the whole time: a dial Nestor already ships, pointed at the candidate scan best_sealed already uses.
decisions.doors_closed: A different matcher for the decision domain — StringMatcher is sufficient when the bar is calibrated. Semantic embeddings remain the tail fix for the ~25% with too little character overlap (docs/decision-rewording-bench.md §100–113).

decisions.question: What should the default fuzzy_bar be for decision check?
decisions.commitment: 0.55 — the triage calibrate's knee for the full dogfood corpus. The rewording bench's 0.45 was measured on 24 distinct decisions; on 418 decisions with many similarly-shaped questions, 0.45 produces skeleton false-positives (the same finding nestor.triage recorded). 0.55 eliminates observed wrong-keys while recovering close paraphrases (0.68+ correct matches observed). Configurable via --fuzzy-bar on the CLI, and fuzzy_bar= on the DecisionMemory constructor.
decisions.why: Tested empirically on the dogfood corpus: at 0.50, a wrong-key surfaced ('What matcher should the decision domain use?' matched 'What is the missing guard...' at 0.568). At 0.55, that wrong-key disappears and all correct matches (0.68+) remain. The triage module independently found 0.55 as the knee via --calibrate sweep. Consistent with the bench's principle: calibrate per corpus, not one number for all.
decisions.doors_closed: 0.45 as the default on a 418-decision corpus — measured to produce wrong-keys from question-scaffold overlap.
